items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I joined Russell's orchestra... The others were Charlie Holmes, alto... Henry 'Moon' Jones had replaced Charlie Holmes on alto sax

ctx.x: woman that Mack Walker and I had stayed with before for my wife and myself. We could cook there and that was much better than having to eat in restaurants and cheaper for two people.

I joined Russell's orchestra which was composed of mostly musicians from New Orleans. And those that were not were strangers to me. There was Henry 'Red' Allen, trumpet, Albert Nicholas, alto and clarinet but he played clarinet most of the time, George 'Pops' Foster whom I had seen carrying a bass violin once but had never met him. Paul Barbarin was the drummer. They were all from New Orleans. The others were Charlie Holmes, alto, Teddy Hill, tenor sax, and Higgy who was the only one I knew.
Metcalf had left the band, I was told, because Russell had sent for Red Allen when he went into the Roseland and Red played too much horn to suit Metcalf, so he quit.

items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: Bill Coleman was on trumpet. Bill Coleman was with us once.

ctx.x: No, no, it wasn't him. He's been around. Good bass player. He still works around. Let me see. Bill Coleman was on trumpet. Bill Coleman was with us once. I'm trying to think, was he with... I don't know if Bill Coleman was with Kirby or Billy Kyle. Because Bill Coleman worked in one of the bands, and Wallace Jones worked in one of the bands. I forget which was which.
See, because Kirby had been in the place, and then he come out, I think he was out about two weeks, and then Billy taken the band in there. It was practically the same men,
